body: As a private guide with over 20 years of experience in Sri Lanka’s Cultural Triangle, I have climbed the steps to the Dambulla Cave Temple hundreds of times, and it remains one of my favorite places to show guests.This isn't just a temple; it is an art gallery carved into rock. The complex consists of five main caves, each filled with stunning Buddha statues and ceiling paintings that date back centuries. The colors and details, preserved inside the cool caves, are incredible to see in person.Tips for Future Visitors:Buy Tickets at the Bottom: This is the #1 mistake travelers make! The ticket counter is at the bottom of the hill (near the Golden Temple statue). If you climb the stairs without a ticket, you will have to go all the way back down.The Climb: It is roughly 360 steps (about 15-20 minutes). It is not extremely difficult, but it can be hot. Take your time and enjoy the view of Sigiriya Rock in the distance from the top terrace.Dress Code: You must cover shoulders and knees. I always recommend my guests bring a sarong or scarf to wrap around before entering the courtyard.Watch the Monkeys: The path is full of toque macaque monkeys. They are fun to watch, but do not feed them or carry plastic bags with food, as they can be cheeky.Whether you are interested in history, art or Buddhism, Dambulla is unmissable. I recommend visiting in the late afternoon (around 4:00 PM) when the light is golden and the heat has gone down. A truly spiritual experience.
title: Why Dambulla is a Must-Visit & How to Do It Right

body: PRO TIP: SAVE YOUR LEGS! THE SECRET SHORTCUT TO THE TOPAvoid the main, long, steep staircase entirely! Most visitors waste huge amounts of energy on the primary path, but there's a detour that cuts off almost 70% of the climbing effort.After buying your ticket near the Archaeological Museum, ask a local or tuk-tuk driver to point you toward the "easier road" or the "security hut" near the giant seated Golden Buddha statue. There is a cement-inclined road that dramatically cuts the ascent. Use this path to get straight to the upper complex entrance.Dambulla is more than a destination; it’s a portal into history. While the large Golden Temple complex at the base is impressive, the real magic—and the part that deserves the attention—is up the ancient rock.The effort to reach the top is profound, and what truly took my breath away was the atmosphere and the art inside the five main caves: Devaraja Viharaya, Maharaja Viharaya, Maha Alut Viharaya, Paschima Viharaya, and Devana Alut Viharaya.The Standout Experience:You climb the rock in Sri Lanka's intense heat, and when you finally remove your shoes and step under the cave overhang, the temperature drops instantly. You transition from the harsh sun to a dim, cool, incense-scented silence.Inside the five main caves, the sense of scale is overwhelming. The ceilings aren't flat, plastered canvases—they are the natural, curved rock face, painted over with an astonishing, unbroken fresco covering over 2,100 square meters. It feels less like a series of caves and more like being inside the mind of the Buddha itself, where every surface, curve, and crack tells a story.What Makes It Unique (Look for These Insider Details!):• Cave 2 (Maharaja Viharaya): This is the largest cave and holds the most secrets:• The First Flag & Great Battle: Look for the mural depicting the great battle between King Elara and King Dutugamunu. Look very closely for the flag King Dutugamunu is carrying—it is believed to be one of the earliest representations of the Sri Lankan flag! Its location is roughly parallel to the water pot.• The Gunman Proof: In the spectacular Maraparajaya mural (Temptation of Mara), look for the highly unusual detail of a man holding a gun in the far right corner. This detail is key proof that the murals belong to the 17th-19th century Kandyan era, as guns were introduced then. This mural is one of only two known to exist in the entire country with this detail!• Royal Statues: Near the second entrance, find the statue of King Valagamba (the temple’s founder), and note the restricted corner where the statue of King Nissankamalla (the 12th-century restorer) is situated.• Rare Buddha Posture: Look for the standing Buddha painted orange with crossed hands—a rare position depicting universal kindness.• Cave 4 (Paschima Viharaya): Look for the small stupa here, named Somawathi Stupa, which scholars believe once contained the jewelry of King Valagamba’s Queen Somawathi. Notice the line of separation on the plaster: the lower part is the original, and the upper part was replaced after the stupa was sadly robbed in centuries past.• Cave 5 (Devana Alut Viharaya): At the very far right end of the back wall, search for the unique black mural of the god Vishwakaruna Divya puthra, who is responsible for arts and music.Quick Tip for Visitors:• Timing: Go as early as possible (opens at 7 AM) to beat the heat and the tour bus crowds.• The View: Don't rush past the top terrace! On a clear day, the panoramic view gives you a perfect perspective of the flat plains stretching out, with the famous Sigiriya Rock Fortress visible in the distance—it's a great payoff after the climb.

body: Huge car park with clean toilets available for tourists and few drinks/ snack stalls . Tickets 3000 SLR per person paid cash on the first level of flight of stairs . body: I visited the Dambulla Golden Temple during my holiday in Sri Lanka and it was one of the most peaceful and inspiring moments of my trip. The temple is located on a small hill, and after a short climb, you’re rewarded with breathtaking views and a truly unique cultural site.Inside the cave temple, I was amazed by the number of beautifully preserved Buddha statues — over 150 in total — and the stunning ceiling murals that are centuries old. Each of the five caves tells a different story through its artwork and atmosphere. It felt like stepping into a sacred time capsule.The place is well maintained, and there is a deep sense of calm once you step inside. Even with other visitors around, the atmosphere remained quiet and respectful. I recommend wearing comfortable shoes for the walk up and bringing water, especially if you’re visiting during the hotter hours.This UNESCO World Heritage Site is a must for anyone interested in history, spirituality, or architecture. It’s not just a tourist stop — it’s a meaningful experience. Definitely worth the visit!

body: A fascinating place to understand a little more of Sri Lankan history and beliefs. The details in the statues and frescoes is beautiful - and great to see restoration work underway A few points (many covered by previous reviews):- the caves are not ground level. You do need to walk up a steady incline of steps. The steps are wide and there are handrails. - you will be expected to donate for using washrooms in the parking area; for flowers to offer the Buddha if you wish to take some; to the shoe minders at the top- make sure your shoulders and knees are covered. A simple scarf or wrap across your shoulders is fine. If you don’t have appropriate clothing you can hire covers for a fee- you do leave your shoes to go into the temple area. The ground was very hot where not under shade (we were there around 11.30am). You can wear socks which is a good option I allowed an hour for our visit including walking up and back) and that was sufficient.

body: You must walk 400 steps vertically before you enter. This can be extremely dehydrating due to the heat so prepare yourself. Some say 10min, others say 20min. Entirely depends on your level of fitness. Counted the steps, there are 400. You must purchase ticket at the bottom of the steps, or about 20 steps up on left. Find the booth though as the location does change regularly. Take socks (hot ground) and a spare bag for shoes if you do not want to pay for storage, as you will be directed to do so. You must go shoeless, no exceptions. You must cover your knees, down over calfs. You must cover your arms. No exceptions. You will have to pay for shoulder and leg covers if you are not dressed appropriately, or no entrance. When in, you will be harassed by guides, asked for donations etc. It is what it is. The caves. They're steeped in history and have budda's and wall paintings. They're severely needing maintenance though and you have to question where all the entrance fee money, shoe storage money, shoulder and leg covering money is going...as it's not on maintenance. There is no facilities at top, toilets are at bottom and no exit after entry.Oh it also shuts down from 1030 - 1045am daily for some worship. If you're in a cave, you are locked in so plan accordingly!Is it worth it? Of course, it's a world heritage site. It's just not maintained or treated like one from the staff/local community. Shame.

body: The Dambulla Cave Temple, also known as the Golden Temple of Dambulla, is one of Sri Lanka’s most impressive and well-preserved cave temple complexes. Nestled atop a massive rock, this UNESCO World Heritage Site features five intricately decorated caves filled with stunning murals and over 150 statues of Buddha, some dating back to the 1st century BCE.The temple offers breathtaking views of the surrounding countryside, making the climb up even more rewarding. The intricate paintings and serene atmosphere create a sense of awe and spirituality. It’s a must-visit for history lovers, culture enthusiasts, and anyone seeking a peaceful yet visually stunning experience in Sri Lanka.
title: Dambulla cave Temple

body: The Dambulla Cave Temple, also known as the Golden Caves of Infinite Buddhas, is a remarkable UNESCO World Heritage Site located 148km from Colombo. This ancient rock temple, with a history dating back to the 1st Century BC, offers a fascinating glimpse into Sri Lanka's rich cultural past.The temple consists of five main caves, each filled with stunning statues and vibrant paintings. Cave No. 1 features a 47-foot long reclining Buddha, a magnificent sight that is believed to have been crafted by divine hands. Cave No. 2, the largest and most impressive, houses 150 life-size Buddha statues and colorful ceiling murals depicting significant events from Buddha's life and Sri Lankan history.Cave No. 3, built during the Kandyan period, showcases 57 Buddha statues and intricate paintings from the era, offering a glimpse into the island's last kingdom before British colonization. Cave No. 4 is said to be where King Valagamba lived during his exile, and it contains a small dagoba with a storied past. Cave No. 5, added during the British period, features a reclining Buddha and several other statues, making it a fascinating mix of cultural influences.Visiting the Dambulla Cave Temple is like stepping back in time, with each cave revealing layers of history, spirituality, and artistry. It's a must-see for anyone exploring Sri Lanka.

body: My inaugural day in Sri Lanka was a magical immersion into the ancient wonders of Dambulla Cave Temple. Nestled amidst lush greenery, this UNESCO World Heritage site is a treasure trove of art, history, and spirituality.As I ascended the steps to the cave entrance, I was greeted by breathtaking panoramic views of the surrounding landscape. Stepping inside, I was immediately captivated by the intricate cave paintings and sculptures adorning the rock walls, each telling a story of devotion and artistic mastery that has endured for centuries.Exploring the five caves felt like stepping into a sacred sanctuary, where the air was imbued with a sense of reverence and tranquility. The sight of the towering Buddha statues, illuminated by soft shafts of sunlight filtering through the cave openings, left me in awe of the ancient artisans who created such masterpieces.Outside the caves, the sprawling temple complex offered further opportunities for discovery, with serene courtyards and vibrant shrines inviting quiet contemplation and reflection.The entrance fee was 6 USD per adult, which I found to be a small price to pay for the priceless experience of exploring this extraordinary site.My experience at Dambulla Cave Temple was nothing short of transformative, leaving me with a deep appreciation for Sri Lanka's rich cultural heritage and spiritual legacy. It's a destination that beckons travelers to embark on a journey of discovery and enlightenment, and I feel privileged to have had the opportunity to explore its hallowed halls
title: Sacred Serenity: Exploring Dambulla Cave

body: We had our driver with us to act as guide to the caves. This was a do not miss part of our journey around Sri Lanka. Very busy so go as early as you can, expect to be impressed, and wear comfortable footwear, there are many steps.
title: Fabulous but busy, go as early as you can, lots of steps..

body: The place itself is great and magical. There are 4 caves filled with ancient Buddha statues, statues of ancient kings and some Indian gods.Unfortunately, there is no additional information about the place (like labels), and you need to have a guide to understand the context.We had to hire local guide (as we were told we can’t enter with our own) and this was not a nice experience. He rushed us through the caves in 10 minutes, talking incredibly fast, just wishing to finish as soon as possible. While we were walking in the caves after “our tour” we saw some decent guides showing and explaining all kind of symbols to other lucky visitors. Therefore we still don’t know if we were so unlucky with the local guide or we could bring some guide with proper license from outside. If you look down the hill there are lots of plastic bottles and trash. Considering the ticket price, it could be cleaned. We left with a feeling that this wonderful place is solely used to get the tourist money.
title: Ancient beautiful place but sadly used as a tourist ripp off

body: Incredibly hot inside, and if the humidity is high this will get to you as there’s no ventilation system at all. Bring a fan or a booklet or something you can use as one. Lighting is amazing and the exhibits are truly stunning. Would definitely be better to experience with a guide, which we , and ended up being in and out in about half an hour cuz almost no explanatory plaques at all.
title: Hot but worth it: bring a fan and a guide

body: Magnificent temple not to be missedThe sculptures are splendid and the colors incredible.You can access from one side (jungle side) or the other (golden temple)
title: Splendid temple not to be missed

body: A very beautiful site, carefully maintained, I think it is the most beautiful of all the ones I have seen.These ceilings and walls decorated with such care and harmony, wonderful
title: Marvelous

body: A very interesting site with a lot of history attached to it. There are four temples to go into and they are simply magical - we had a guide explaining lots to us which was very worthwhile.
title: Well worth a visit

body: I understand the cultural significance but this is an overpriced place of worship that shouldn't even charge people. It was priced the same as the Temple of the Tooth in Kandy which was much larger with actual information provided for you to learn from and several museums. The Dambulla cave is also priced at 1500 lkr on the Sigiriya Fortress government website but they charge 2000 lkr at the site (with no option to pre-book). I also didn't like to be forced to remove my shoes and charged to leave them on a shoe rack, this should be included in the exorbitant entrance fee.
title: Possibly worth skipping

body: Well worth a visit and good value at around £5/2000 rupees. Both men and women must cover their legs. If you forget sarongs are provided with hilarious consequences especially for the men. It's 100 rupees for the covering .Socks are not provided but recommended as the tiles/floor/rock can get seriously hot. Again hilarious consequences. Think Squid Games ...
title: Must visit in Dambulla

body: It’s a stiff climb up a lot of steps but well worth it. Fantastic statues in cave temples and lovely painted walls and ceilings carved from the rock. Impressive gold Buddha statue to see on the way down.
title: Worth the climb

body: After a climb of around 300 steps a terrace offers a very nice view. The 5 caves to visit are aligned along a rock wall. They house some 150 Buddhas in different sizes and sizes. Cave number 2 is the largest of the 5. Superb ceiling entirely painted with small Buddhas. In the center of the room a jar has been collecting water falling drop by drop for 22 centuries! All the caves feature reclining Buddhas, murals and painted ceilings.
title: After the effort, the reward!

body: Also known as the Golden Temple of Dambulla, Also a UNESCO heritage site.It is the largest cave temple in Sri Lanka with 5 caves, boasting 153 statues of Buddha, The largest is 52 meters long and 7 maters high. There are also with statues of kings, gods and goddesses. The Buddha’s are mainly depicting Gautama Buddha’s life. The walls and ceilings are also covered in frescoes, a very impressive sight. The entrance fee is 2000 like, which at the time our visit was £5, very reasonable we thought.There is an impressive gold Buddha.Remember that the knee and shoulders need to be covered to visit the temple.At the front there is an impressive gold Buddha statue, the gold temple, we drove to the rear and there is a stairway from the ticket office with around 400 stairs, which is the easier option of entrance, there are monkeys to see along the way, it’s not too strenuous at a leisurely pace, mostly in the shade of trees too. At the top there is a kiosk to leave your shoes while you visit the caves.An impressive attraction which should be visited while in Sri Lanka, would definitely recommend.
title: Impressive Caves

body: Very beautiful place with a total of 160 Buddha statues. The stairs are a bit tiring but easily doable - beautiful view
title: Beautiful cave temples

body: A very steep climb up hundreds of steps to the top but worth the effort. The cave temples and wall paintings were amazing to say they have lasted through all those centuries. Men need to wear long trousers or cut offs below the knee and maybe wear socks if you have sensitive feet as you remove your footwear before entering.
title: Amazing Cave Temples

body: Very fascinating rock temple. We visited it in the early afternoon, so the climb took our legs a little, after inside the caves the hot, still air didn't help us.The 5 caves are home to more than one hundred Buddhas, in all positions: even the painted ceilings are stunning.
title: Buddha in all poses, painted on the ceilings.....endlessly!

body: There are two ways to climb up to see the caves. The main entrance is where you will find the ticket office. Entrance is $10 per adult. You are then presented with a climb of 200 steps on stone steps. There are rest places along the climb but no bannister to hold on to. Some of the steps are quite steep. If you’re not good with doing this then buy your ticket and get your driver to take you to the Golden Temple ( just round the corner from the Rock Cave car park). To the left of the Golden Temple you will see a sign -To The Rock Temple- this is a more sedate climb and the steps are more even and made of concrete. Don’t make the mistake of heading to the Golden Temple steps without buying a ticket first otherwise you will get to the top and will be denied entrance and directed to go down the stone steps to the ticket office. It’s hot work without having to descend to buy a ticket!! Once you are at the top there is a spectacular view.
title: Top tip for climbing to the caves

body: The ascent takes approximately 15 minutes at a normal pace.The temple is very interesting - the halls are carved into the rock.Of course, you need to go with a guide who will tell interesting stories.The view of the surrounding area from the hill is impressive.The hot stones in front of the temple entrance can only cause discomfort if the sun is too hot, because... On the territory of the temple and in the temple you can only walk barefoot (you can also wear socks).
title: Dambulla Cave Temple

body: The walk up is a moderate one and can be done on two sides of the hillock. The paintings on the huge rock ceiling of the cave temple are fascinating.The ticket counter closes at 5pm. Shorts not allowed... advisable to carry a wrap-around cloth while visiting temples.
title: Divine Cavern

body: Dambulla Cave Temple is a very peaceful and calm place. I really like visiting this temple. This is UNESCO world heritage site number 561.There is a bit of a steep hill to climb to get to the entrance, so if you are handicapped, you may not be able to do it. I just wanted to mention this because we had a person who walks with a cane and she could not do it.There is an entrance fee of Rs 2,000 for each foreigner (non Sri Lankan citizen) to enter, they will give you a ticket after you pay (see picture). My wife is a Sri Lankan citizen and there was no fee for her. I’m actually Sri Lankan, but if you look like you don’t live here, they will ask for proof that you live here. Don’t cause problems, just pay the Rs 2,000 or approximately USD $6, it’s worth it.Like all Buddhist temples in Sri Lanka, you must remove your shoes before entering. This place can get crowded, so if you do not want to wait in line to leave your shoes with the people who will watch them for you or if you have some expensive shoes and you are worried about leaving them, then carry a simple shopping bag with you and place your shoes inside the bag before entering, you can carry the bag inside with no problems. Also, you cannot wear shorts and a tank top, you must have covered shoulders and your knees covered. If you attempt to go inside without these areas covered they will give you something that you must wear to cover up. These are handed from person to person, so if you are concerned about germs, then wear appropriate clothing before you go.The day we visited it started raining when we were about to leave and we got soaking wet because there is a bit of a walk down the hill to the car. I recommend you take an umbrella with you if it looks like it may rain.I have no complaints about this place and look forward to visiting again.
title: Amazing and Peaceful Temple

body: Most certainly worth a visit to this world heritage site. Just be aware of the climb up and the need to have knees and shoulders covered, so bring trousers, a sarong or similar. They ask you to put your shoes in storage, then 200 rupees to get them back at the end. That isnt much and our thoughts are, it goes towards the temple and creates jobs. You can take photos but not with your back to a Buddha, it is rude to do so as your backside is facing Buddha. Enjoy your visit.
title: Well worth a visit but bring your trou!

body: It was a pleasure to see this piece of Sri Lankan history. My guide was very knowledgeable and explained details of the Sri Lankan dynasty and culture of 'wishing' to give thanks after a wish has come true and donate an effigy of Budha. It is a long climb up large steps so do pace yourself. There is are places to rest on the way up. The views are spectacular and a serene place.
title: Exceptional historic experience

body: I went to see the beautiful cave temples in Dambulla. There are quite a few steps leading to beautiful temple area. The walls are frescoed. There are many statues of the Buddha. The views are also beautiful from the top.
title: Beautiful cave temple from 80 BC

body: Very suggestive sacred place: a series of rooms dug into the side of a mountain in different periods and renovated without however compromising the suggestiveness of the site. The second environment is the largest and also the richest: the eye is lost among the rock frescoes, the dozens of statues, the stupa, the "perennial drop" that marked the meditation of the monks who lived here. Take your time and explore all the corners (even the soles of the reclining Buddha's feet in the first cave!). Shoes are left after the long access staircase, before entering the sacred area; and you must have your legs covered and, for women, your arms too.
title: Not to be missed

body: This is really a stunning site, an ancient cave full of statues of Buddha and other deities. Even more awe inspiring that it’s been around for 22 centuries. Definitely worth a visit!A couple of tips - there is a fair bit to climb, not really a hike but can easily get winded. Having said that, the views when you get to the top are lovely (including Sigiriya and Pidurangala). There are two entrances. If you enter from the temple side, you have to climb up, and then go all the way to the bottom of the other side to buy tickets (LKR 2,000 only for foreigners). The guy at the ticket counter didn’t have change and fairly dismissively told me to wait till someone else happened to come along so he could get change, so I wasn’t too pleased about that. There are no tickets at the top! Wonderfully majestic and really an impressive sight.
title: Impressive ancient cave temple

body: Incredible series of caves with frescoes and wood and stone statues. Very knowledgeable guide. We were a bit rushed to see it all because they were closing the doors for prayer.This was an extra on our tour and I'm so pleased we didn't miss it.Very reasonable tourist entrance fee compared to the better known sites.Don't miss it.
title: Must see cave temples

body: As many reviews have described it is best to enter from the rear side (not the Golden Buddha side). There is ample parking then a sign indicating a few steps up to the ticket office. From there is 400 rough steps to the cave temples. Most stairs are under tree shade. Close to the top is an old local lady sells flowers to place at Buddha cost LKR200. We placed them then the cleaner picked them up and threw them in the bin - perhaps our timing was unlucky. Also at the top is a shoe kiosk where you pay by donation. Being our first day we had no idea of the local currency so paid a donation of LKR2000 for 2 pairs of shoes. The man was very pleased and shook my hand with a big smile as the going rate is probably 100. Oh well it was a good day for him and his family. A TIP is to keep your socks on as the stone ground gets hot. We also paid a local just inside the entry to the temple to give us a talk but it was fairly basic. I think getting some information from he internet would have been better.We then came back down the same stairs to the car park, meet our private driver who then drove us around to the Golden Buddha. We went up the stairs but really the best viewing is down the bottom. Didn't go in the museum so can't comment about that.
title: Worth the 400 steps

body: You start by climbing the stairs. You emerge from roads with magnificent views. You can leave your bags at the safe deposit box at the first entrance. When you reach the temple at the top, you will encounter a wonderful architecture. For a very small fee, you can have a local prayer to ward off bad luck read and a rope tied around your wrist.
title: Amazing Place

body: The steep walk up is very worthwhile however our driver did not inform us that we needed to cover up so we had to hire a sarong plus have money to store our shoes. Once inside the cave temples are spectacular and very unique and I highly recommend viewing.
title: Worth a visit but be prepared

body: The Dambulla Cave Temple in Sri Langka is a sacred pilgrimage site for 22 centuries. This cave monastery has 5 cave sanctuaries and the best preserved cave temple complex in Sri Lanka. The mural paintings on the walls cover an area of 2,100 meters.
title: Cave temple

body: One of the visits that fascinated us the most.These are 5 caves with dozens of Buddha statues inside in various positions and completely frescoed with images of the Buddha's life.The ticket can be purchased directly at the ticket office located at the beginning of the steps and is more than cheap, 2000 rupees.After the ticket office, a long staircase begins, mostly in the sun.Be careful of the monkeys, they are ready to steal anything that is left unattended.Before entering the temple you must take off your shoes, you can leave them in a deposit by paying 50 rupees.This is a sacred place, shoulders and knees must be covered.It's a good idea to take at least a couple of hours to visit all the caves and admire the attention to detail of the statues and frescoes.Furthermore, from the top it is possible to enjoy a splendid view of the valley.An unmissable visit, in our opinion the most beautiful temple we have seen in Sri Lanka.
title: Wonderful rock temple

body: 390 steps up but the caves are well worth a visit. Some great painting inside with multiple Buddha statues. Watch out for the monkey poo on the steps.
title: Worth a visit

body: This was our first stop of our 3 day tour of Sri Lanka there's me and my wife she's uses a wheelchair So we arrived and we had to walk up the hills to get to the top it took 3 of us to push my wife up the steep hills so we got up there it's very busy lots of locals praying lots to see and lots of history we was grateful that we saw this and recommend it
title: Amazing site

body: Most popular and an ancient temple in Dambulla town. This temple is very famous amount the locals and touriest as well.Very calm and silent place for meditation.Community from all religion visits here without any difference. All the necessary facilities are available.
title: Must Visit Place

body: You have to climb a lot of stairs to climb to the top (I counted 470) and it is mandatory to take off your shoes before entering the temple (poor feet!!)The show you will find will make up for everything5 caves with 153 Buddhas of all sizes insideA mystical place
title: Mystical

body: Superb temple made up of 5 caves, differently decorated.Entrance 2000 rps per person + tips for leaving your shoes.
title: Unmissable

body: Dambulla and its quarries will remain etched in my memory. They are absolutely spectacular and worth seeing. Include this visit in your tour of Sri Lanka because it is definitely worth it. You will be amazed when you see the paintings and statues. Wonderful atmosphere!
title: Wonderful Dambulla

body: "We had the incredible opportunity to visit the Dambulla Cave Temple, and it truly exceeded all expectations. Nestled within the lush landscape of Sri Lanka, this ancient marvel is a testament to the country's rich cultural and historical heritage. The intricate cave paintings and sculptures, some dating back over two thousand years, are a mesmerizing sight to behold. As you ascend the steps to the temple, the panoramic views of the surrounding countryside are breathtaking. The serene atmosphere and spiritual aura of the temple create a sense of tranquility and introspection. Whether you're a history enthusiast, an art lover, or simply seeking a unique and meaningful experience, the Dambulla Cave Temple is an absolute must-visit destination."
title: Amazing ancient city

body: An ancient temple to view Buddha statues preserved in a cave. One of culturally important location and must visit if you are a tourist. Highly recommend.
title: Great experience.

body: Relatively easy walk up, great views. The temples themselves were interesting but quite busy. As at other sights, enjoyment and understanding depends on the quality of the guide. Although our guide knowledgeable it was a prepared script with no room for deviation!
title: Worth the climb

body: Absolutely loved the UNESCO World Heritage Cave Temples in Dambulla. We did it the same day as Sigiriya Rock so after a 1200 step climb in Sigiriya, it was a 600 step climb up Dambulla. If you are in the area longer then doing it on two different days, would be better. If not, do it on the same day and do not miss seeing the caves. There are five main caves that you can see. You can take photographs inside the caves too but do not use flash photography inside to preserve the frescos and the serene atmosphere inside the caves. My tour guide seemed to indicate that there were no rules against flash photography (he may be mistaken) but I did not use any flash photography inside. The frescos are painted on the walls and the ceilings and are absolutely awesome to see in the dim light in the caves. Give yourself about 2 hours to see the place.There are places while climbing the steps where you can pause, take some pics and give your legs a little rest before proceeding up. There is a place to leave your footwear, a little away from the caves. There is also a small entrance fee to enter the caves. Also they do close the caves for 15-20 minutes in the morning - I think at 10 am for worship of the Buddha statues inside the caves. So be aware of that. We saw 2 caves and then had to wait outside till they reopened to see the other 3 caves.Sigiriya Rock and Dambulla Caves both are absolutely awesome and must not be missed if you are visiting the area.
title: Must visit Cave Temples

body: On the 2nd day of our Holidays in Sri Lanka and after visiting Pinnawalla Elephant Orphanage, we proceed to visit Dambulla Cave Temple which is also known as Golden Temple. This Buddhist Temple Complex which is situated on top of mountain approximately 160 meters above the plains and is also a World Heritage site.It consists of five main caves, which house numerous statues and paintings related to Buddhism. These caves have a history dating back more than 2,000 years and have been continuously occupied by Buddhist monks. These Caves have a large number of Statues of Lord Buddha in various forms along with various other deities and important figures from Buddhist history. The walls and ceilings of the caves are adorned with vibrant frescoes depicting scenes from the life of Buddha and other religious motifs along with that of Hindu Deity, Lord Vishnu.At the entrance of the Complex, one can see the renowned Grand Golden Buddha Statue which has been well preserved along with other artefacts and attract large number of Pilgrims as well as Tourists from Srilanka and World over.
title: Dambulla Golden Temple

body: Beautiful cave temples with lot of history. We chose to trek up 360 odd steep steps to reach the temples and exit using the pathway with a quick stop at the golden Buddha temple. The Dambulla cave temple gates shut at 6pm.
title: Two ways to reach this temple - stairs or inclined pathway.

body: I was apprehensive about climbing the stairs as I have damaged knees. However, our driver dropped us off at another pathway which was more like ramps, making the ascent easier. The five caves were worth the trek, with their sacred Buddhist images dating from C3rd BC to modern times.We used the stairs to descend and I noticed that some of them didn't have handrails, which was my only complaint. It would be wonderful if they could transport people to the caves without the stairs at some point in the future.
title: Worth the 360 stairs

body: When you walk up the hill and see this Temple - amazing - but when you go inside there's nothing that will prepare you for the beauty and amazing painting, statues etc inside the rooms. I hadn't done any research on it and loved it.
title: Gobsmacking!

body: Amazing monastery complex belongs to 3 rd Bc,it s contain 05 caves connect to each other,hundreds of different kinds posture of load budha statures.
title: Nissanka malla inscription belong to 16 th century mentioned how to do the rituals & protect .

body: This is must visit attraction in Sri Lanka. The hike to the caves is exciting and the views from top are mesmerizing. The cave temple is serene and calm offering plethora of Lord Buddha statues in different forms and positions.
title: Must visit attraction

body: Absolutely amazing site 5 caves full of artefacts and painted walls and roofs, on a hot and humid day a decent level of fitness is required are there are quite a few tiers of steps to reach the caves but well worth the effort.
title: Amazing cave complex

body: Nice spot to visit - less than 30 minutes away from Sigiriya's center. You take stairs up to the temple where you deposit your shoes and can walk barefoot into the temple. It is a cluster of temples and you can walk from one to the other. Have something on you to cover your knees (males and females) and shoulders and socks because the floor is hot. There's an entry ticket and a fee to deposit your shoes. More reviews @myra.recommends
title: Nice spot

body: Beautiful place, well maintained. Would definitely wow those who love history and buddhism. Worth a visit just to understand local culture.
title: Local Buddhism and History

body: This is a very ancian monastery in sri lanka. If you are interesting to learn about buddism or want to do researches please visit this place
title: Reaserchers can get help on buddism

body: Bit of a steep climb to get to the caves but the views from the top are worth it. I have seen many temples / shrines etc over the years across the world so its easy to get blasé about another temple / statue but I would recommend visiting here as the caves are quite unique. The paintings & statues are interesting and this is obviously a very special place for Buddhists. Beware of the monkeys - they are everywhere & pinch anything !
title: Worth a visit (even if you are 'templed out!')

body: amazing place. Five caves it is a beautiful . Amazing wall paint. Dont mis it your tours in srilanka
title: Amazing place to see it

body: Peaceful place with beautiful surroundings, monkeys. Have never seen something like that, very special energy of the place.
title: Worth travelling to see it your own eyes

body: Have to climb some steps but I will tell you this is one of the beautiful Buddhist temples I have seen in my entire life. Beautiful paintings and great statues. More than 150 paintings also pleasure to see
title: Amazing place

body: Must to see amazing temple , so kind person and highly recomended place to see , kids are visiting and learning also taining in temple
title: Amazing

body: Quite a few steps to climb but worth it. The statues and paintings in the rock temples are amazing. The temples are actually set in natural rock caves with walls built in front to seal off the temple. Suggest good footwear.
title: Amazing rock temples

body: This almost thousand year old temple was built by a grateful king who was given shelter by Buddhist monks when he was on the run from enemy armies.The paintings look like they were painted only yesterday but in reality they are many centuries old.The temple is very well maintained and is a sacred place for Buddhists.The staff are polite and friendly. They waited patiently for us to see all the caves before closing the temple complex for the day.The approach to the temple has been very well maintained with chiseled steps, handrails, lights and resting places.It is suggested that a cable car system could be installed for the pilgrims who are unable to climb all those steps.The temple is in excellent condition and the rock temple is a beautiful place to visit and meditate.A must visit while you are in Dambulla, Sri Lanka.Highly recommended.
title: A grateful king's tribute to his saviours a thousand year ago.

body: Dabulla cave temple is a place of cultural value in our country. It feels a bit tiring while climbing the steps, but when you climb to the top of the rock, you can see the beautiful view. Then we explored the cave paintings and sculptures.
title: Explore the natural caves

body: A little bit of a climb up the road and a visit to five ancient caves was worthwhile. It was our first temple visit so interesting enough with many ancient Buddha statues. A bit different being constructed within the natural caves.
title: Worth a short visit

body: Visited the cave complex from Habarana for a few hours after a day by the pool. Easy to get to by bus (45/48 from Habarana junction in direction of Kandy) but make sure they let you off by the front of the golden Buddha rather than in town (my conductor refused for some reason which meant a bit of a long walk). As others have said I can highly recommend getting a tuk tuk round to the ticket office then it’s only a short climb up to the top (15 mins). Once you are up there the views are epic, if you go late afternoon (around 4.30pm for me) there are not too many people around so easier to see the caves properly. Suggesting starting from the furthest cave and working your way back towards the entrance as this gives you more of a build up. Caves were impressive and had a really peaceful atmosphere, highly recommended. Afterwards just head down main staircase and flag down a bus going back your direction from the road.
title: Great way to spend a few hours

body: Beautifull caves, a guide is needed for full value due to the complex history. Few visitors due to the current situation.
title: Must see

body: As this is a temple be prepared to dress appropriately, knees and shoulders covered for both men and women. Note that unlike some temples around the world there is no option outside the temple to hire a sarong type thing to cover up with. Plan your day accordingly and do what we did, which was to do a quick change in to long pants inside our van prior to heading to the temple, our last activity for the day. We had a guide which was organised by our driver, he was very good sharing extensive knowledge throughout the various caves. Be mindful when taking photos as it is disrespectful to face your back to Buddha, so don’t try and take selfies with Buddha in the background. You need to leave your shoes outside with attendants who charge you a small donation fee, you pay the fee on retrieval of your shoes so have some small change on you. The caves are amazing and will take approx an hour at the most depending on how much your guide likes to talk to complete the caves. Another must see while in Sri Lanka.
title: Terrific Temple.

body: About 340 steps which is a seamless climb. Five ancient caves with painted ceilings and walls, and Buddhist statues. Peaceful atmosphere and nice visit.If you are planning a visit, read on:1. One can use footwear and safely deposit them right outside the temple.2. Monkeys are common on the climb up and do come close to tourists expecting food. Do not feed them and neither try to attack them since they get aggressive quickly. Simply walk past and ensure no loose hanging bags or cameras are easy to grab for monkeys. Because they ambush and try to steal expecting food. In my case I carried a small wooden stick to pretend warn them and we were alright.3. Once you visit the caves and come out, do not take the same way down. Walk forward and you should see a way to the left leading to the golden buddha statue, a museum, and a book store. Followed by a local snack stall.Have a nice visit and do check out the rock seller on the way down if you fancy a collection like I do. A bit of haggling is all you need to strike a good bargain.
title: Peaceful temple

body: Beautiful Buddhist temple in a peaceful location. Unfortunately only the middle section of the cave was properly lit and the remaining sections were left in the darkLocals enter free of charge and foreigners are charged rs 2000 per head which I thought a bit hefty to visit a place of worship
title: Worth a visit

body: Entry was 2000lkr per person which seems slightly on the expensive side. The cave temples were nice and well maintained however there was little to read in English so without a guide it’s hard to understand what you’re looking at I.e the history behind it. Worth a visit if nearby and have time.
title: A nice visit If passing

body: Was nice to see and learn about Buddhism. Tickets were 2000lkr to enter the temple. Took us about an hour including the climb which was about 6mins. Definitely bring socks to wear at the top when you take your shoes off shoes can be stored for 25lkr. We also paid 1500lkr for a tour with 6 people - he gave us a few facts but it wasn’t in depth as his English wasn’t that good. 5 caves with many statues of The buddha and intricate paintings.
title: Nice to see

body: Lovely set of small temples on top of a hill. The abundance of statues and wall paintings is truly unique and worth a visit. It costs 2000 LKR per ticket (around $10 atm) but it‘s definitely worth it! Tickets can be purchased both at the bottom by the golden temple and at the top. Make sure you bring socks since you have to take off your shoes to walk around the temple grounds and the ground is scorching hot in the sun!
title: Unique temple

body: A knowledgeable guide needed to get the most from this visit. Blessings available as you enter various caves although the latter ones are somewhat underwhelming. Worth a visit though.
title: Need a guide.

body: There is about 700 stairs till you reach the temple. ( a nice FYI)The temple is very interesting and build inside the caves. It has plenty of history which you will need a guide or potentially do a bit of reading beforehand.
title: Buddhas and Stairs

body: Too expensive, we didn‘t go inside. It‘s 2000 rupiens each person.We just walked up the stairs to the rock for free without going inside the temple. The view was nice.
title: Expensive entry price (2000 each person)

body: We found the cave temples quite underwhelming, despite their history. We’re not Buddhists, and have seen quite a lot of temples travelling across Asia – our experience here didn’t feel hugely special. If you’re at Sigiriya for the day, we’d recommend spending more time there and giving these a skip.You’ll need to cover your knees, but can hire a lungi for 100 rupees. As others have said, the climb up is pretty steep, especially if you’ve already done a lot of walking at Sigiriya that day.

body: From the car park, there is a 10-minute walk upstairs, it is steep but mostly in the shade. body: This is a really interesting place. It's a small temple complex at the top of a hill off of the main road through Dambulla town. It is quite a long, steep climb from the Golden Buddha statue up the steps to the caves so take your time. No shoes allowed in the temple area (there's a place to store them outside the entrance) so have some socks with you as it is very hot underfoot. Once you're in, there are five main caves accessed by a small temple facade built into the rock face. In each of the caves there are lots of Buddha statues of various sizes ranging from human sized up to massive lying down Buddhas about 15 metres long. Take a note of the ornately painted cave ceilings too. Depending on when you visit, the monks do occasionally shut the caves for prayer, but no problem it's only for about 15 minutes. Tip - if you're driving or being driven, enter by the rear steps on the access road a little further into town, as this way you pass the ticket office. Otherwise you'll climb all the way up to the entrance and then have to descend by about 100 steps down to buy your ticket, then climb back up again to get in.

body: Dambulla cave temple Alsop known as the Golden Temple of Dambulla is a World Heritage Site (1991) in Sri Lanka, situated in the central part of the country. Dambulla is the largest and best-preserved cave temple complex in Sri Lanka. The rock towers 160 m over the surrounding plains. There are more than 80 documented caves in the surrounding area. Major attractions are spread over five caves, which contain statues and paintings. These paintings and statues are related to Gautama Buddha and his life. There are a total of 153 Buddha statues, three statues of Sri Lankan kings and four statues of gods and goddesses. The latter include Vishnu and the Ganesha. The murals cover an area of 2,100 square metres (23,000 sq ft). Depictions on the walls of the caves include the temptation by the demon Mara, and Buddha's first sermon.The Dambulla cave monastery is still functional and remains the best-preserved ancient edifice in Sri Lanka.Source #WikipediaIt is a must visit as the statues and paintings are such a delight to the eye. The serenity of the place is something not to be missed. It's not a tough climb and can be completed in about 15 mins up and down. We were blessed with light showers which made the climb bit risky, it was indeed worth the effort.

body: This site is also known as the Golden Temple of Dambulla, a UNESCO site, and the largest and best-preserved cave temple complex in Sri Lanka. The climb to the caves can be fairly taxing depending on age and fitness levels, but worth the effort to view this great complex. There are five caves containing in excess of 150 statues, and extensive murals relating to the Gautama Buddha and his life. The caves are formed by a very large overhang in the face of the rock that has been partitioned and now sits behind a structure of white painted arched colonnades and gabled entrances. It is a mystical site. Enjoy wonderful panoramic views outside, the sun shone and the Rock of Sigiriya was visible in the distance. The visit was made more relevant and informative by our excellent tour guide.

body: Dambulla cave temple is the largest cave temple and world heritage site in Sri Lanka. It is known as Golden Rock Dambulla temple, Dambulu Gala (Dambulla rock) and Rangiri Dambulu Viharaya. There are 153 Buddha statues in total along with three statues of Sri Lankan kings and four statues of god and goddess.

body: It was early evening when we arrived at the temple of five caves of varying size and interior dated 1st BC.There are more than 80 caves in the area with the 5 caves most worth viewing. The first king turned the caves into a temple complex and many kings added to it later until the 11th century. It is still a functioning temple complex till this day.The spectacular murals on the ceilings were of sheer magnificence. They depicted Buddha’s life and sermons. The guide pointed out the large statue of the reclining Buddha on his deathbed judging by the way the feet was displayed. Stupas, a hundred small Buddha statues, some gods and goddesses and kings statues were on display. One of the five caves was under repair, and we managed to take a quick look of it. The second cave was the largest and most impressive.They say you must never turn your back to the Buddha when taking a photo. I felt intense spiritual power in these ancient caves and decided against taking any pictures out of respect.There was a small basin with water dripping down from the ceiling that the guide said would never dry up and have healing powers.Once out of the temple caves we realised how the temple was cut out of a massive overhanging rock. We went under a huge Bodhi tree and made a wish. It was just too bad we could not find time to see the ancient Bodhi tree at Anuradhapura. A very moving spiritual experience indeed.

body: On your way to Sigiriya, it is worth stopping over at Dambulla to catch a glimpse of these wonderful cave temples, ironwood forest and rose quartz mountain. This temple was built in the 1st century BC, by King Valagamba. Mahawansa (old book) says about invasion of seven Tamils from South India in Vlagamba’s reign, (103 BC). The king was unable to fight against them so he fled. Driven out of Anuradhapura by Tamil and remained in exile for 14 years. He came to Dambulla and took refuge in the cave for 14 years. In the meantime he collected an army and went back to Anuradhapura and regained the throne and his second reign was (89-77BC). After regaining the power the king wanted to show his gratitude to the temple. He converted this cave into an interior carved beautiful Buddhist temple. Before the valagamba’s arrival, this cave was donated to the Buddhist monks as dwelling place by king Saddhatissa (137-119 BC).Under the drip ledge of the main cave there is a Brahmi letter inscription. Many other King added to it later and by the 11th century, the caves had become a major religious place. King Nissankamalla gilded the caves and added about 70 Buddha statues in 1190 AD. During the 18th century, belong to kandyan period.This complex of the cave at Dambilla is one of the most impressive Buddhist temples in the world with its great number of Buddha statues and more than 20,000 feet paintings.Todat Dambulla is a world heritage site declared by UNESCO in 1991.thank you,Prasad.

body: The Dambulla Cave Temple is reached by climbing a lot of steps. The trick is to make sure you buy your ticket to enter the caves at the bottom of the steps, as it is not obvious this is the process. To enter most Buddhist Temples you need to dress modestly, no exposed shoulders and knees covered - they do rent items to cover you at the temple entrance. You also need to pay to have your shoes minded whilst you are in the temple and the person you pay is very reluctant to give change so make sure you have the exact amount of 25 rupees. The cost to enter the cave is 1500 rupees. There are five caves and they are stocked with many Buddhas in all manner of positions - if you are yet to visit Myanmar, Thailand, or other such Buddhist countries you will be amazed, but to be honest the South East Asian countries have many of these caves and do it all a lot better. It is though an interesting experience to visit this cave temple.
title: Interesting temple cave experience

body: The cave temple complex is around 300 steps from the plains. The ticket price is 1500 Srilankan rupees. Please make sure to cover your legs and shoulders. Incase if you dont cover, they provide some clothes to cover and charge 100 Rs. You have to remove shoes before you enter the temple. There is a shoe stall, you can leave your shoes there, they charge 25 Rs. As soon as you enter, there are tour guides, who will approach you to take the tour with them, they will try to insist on it but decline them politely. Incase if you want to take, fix the price first.There are no written stories about the 5 cave temples, so i guess the tour guides can be helpful, if you really want to know the stories. Orelse you can google about it and find it on wikipedia “Dambulla cave temple” There are around 150 Buddha statues with lot of fresh flowers, some Srilankan Kings and Hindu gods. The paintings on the ceilings, walls are amazing.After you leave the temple, you can take another exit and head down to the Golden Buddha temple where the huge statue of Buddha facing the mountains is astonishing.
