body: The best time to visit the cave is in the morning hours, early you leave better will be the hike up to the cave. Yes, around 600 meters of a hike from the ticket counter will lead you towards the cave. I will not suggest this to people with issues while walking, but for others, you should visit this place. Word of Caution: Stay away from monkeys, they snatch things from tourists. For photographers: do carry a small mini tripod which can be used inside the cave for good pictures as the light inside is really low and the authorities won't allow you to carry a bigger tripods
title: Great place but not for people with walking issues

body: Quite a decent climb to reach the cave temples, a series of temples with carvings and wall paintings built into the rockface.
title: Interesting cave temple

body: The walkway of the steps aren't event and difficult for older person. Need to hold my aunt hand to go up and down. Please remember to wear socks as it'll be hot as need to walk on bare foot.
title: Unique cave

body: Fabulous Buddhist temple carved into rock caves, filled with wall paintings and statues. You remove your shoes on the approach - beware, the path is very hot!Very impressive and well worth the visit. You are allowed to take photos inside. Sad to see some tourists ignoring the request not to take photos with your back to Buddha - this is offensive. As with removing your shoes, these things should be observed as a courtesy to your hosts.
title: Breathtaking

body: You have to walk up a bit but it’s totally worth it! The temple is a must see! As soon as you walk in the temple guide(men in white) will appear. They greet you and start showing you around. STAY AWAY from them they will want money from you! They lead you to believe it’s free and part of temple service but they are crooks working at the temple grounds!
title: Must see but BEWARE of temple guide!!!!

body: This temple gives a wonderful insight into Buddhism. There is a fine reclining Buddha and an uncountable number of images of the Lord Buddha in meditation having attained enlightenment.
title: A Buddhist temple with magnificent devotional cave frescoes

body: Dambulla Cave Temples houses an impressive collection of Buddhas. There is a hike up a number of stairs to reach the entrance. As it is a temple, you will be required to be dressed appropriately with shoulders and knees covered. There are a series of caves which house the Buddhas. Each one is similar. There are guides who are available for a fee to guide you through but this is not necessary. As we visited just after the terrorism incident in SL, the place had very few people visiting so we could take our time in each cave, Recommended.
title: So many Buddhas

body: The place was wonderful. Although caves look more or less the same, we really enjoy the place. On the way you see monkeys and the landscape is breathtaking.
title: Very nice

body: The Dambulla cave temple was about 10 min ride away in Tuk Tuk from main Dambulla town. The Tuk tuk driver charged me Rs. 300/- for one side. The entrance fee was Rs. 500/- for foreigners. And the dress code was full selves and bottom must be below the knee level. At the temple entrance clothes are available to cover up which cost Rs. 50/- per piece in case you forgot to bring something along. Paid guides are also available inside the temple but its a small place so you won't need one. Always remember that turning your back towards Buddha is said to be very disrespectful. There are many caves with Buddha idols and painting in the temple. Outside the temple you will find many locals selling things, but do bargain if you want to purchase something. After visiting the temple you can head over to the Golden Buddha temple which is on the way down from other side, so take the other way down and its the entrance is free of cost there.
title: Nice hike to amazing Dambulla cave temple.

body: A very nice place and a big temple. To arrive to the cave you have to clipm some big steps and pay a fee at the entrance. Do not forget that you have to leave the shoes at the entrance.
title: A very nice place and a big temple

body: To reach the cave, you will have to get up a lot. In the cave, the area is barefoot, so I recommend taking socks. When we were on the ground it was hot so the feet were hot. The place is interesting. The sculptures are laid out in an interesting way in a cave.
title: Interesting cave

body: Over 2000 years historyMany beautiful frescoes and status The mysterious large pot to collect water dripping from the top 365 days but never overflows or get dry
title: The best cave trample on earth with misty

body: me any my friends visited the cave temple on the way to Kandy from Sigiriya,yes reaally amazing cave with many buddha statues,outside the cave very nice view,attractive environment,we reached the top of the cave within 1/2 hrs,morning time is the best time to climb the crock,otherwise feel tired with middy hot
title: great cave with Buddha statues

body: We walked up from the ticket office at the back which is a relatively steep 300 step climb. The caves them selves where really good to look at and bear about, however wear socks as you must remove your shoes and ensure your knees are covered to enter. Without socks the hot floor can be a real pain. Finally take a little cash, 25 rupees for safe keeping of your shoes. (About 12p). Overall an interesting hour, however not spectacular
title: Decent visit

body: After seeing so many Buddhas, our interest was slightly on the wane. The caves are not particularly deep - I was really expecting some kind of grotto. There were various Buddhas of all shapes and sizes around the room and a patterned ceiling, a bit dark for real appreciation. The visit concluded with a giant golden Buddha, must have been 50 feet tall - rather bling.PLEASE NOTE YOU MUST WEAR TROUSERS, OTHERWISE YOU'LL GET DRAWN INTO ANOTHER CON - YOU WILL HAVE TO PAY FOR YOUR SHOES TO BE LOOKED AFTER!
title: IMPRESSIVE CAVES

body: To infer the temple foreigners must pay 1500 LKR per person. The ticket office is a bit hard to find if you start your visit from the main entrance. Inside the caves there are plenty of statues and paintings which are very nice. But at least for us it was not so impressive as we have hoped for
title: Interesting- but not a “must see”

body: It is a great opportunity to learn about some of the culture of Sri Lanka and to see the many Buddha’s that are hundreds of years old. It is a fairly challenging climb up steps to reach the cave, but it’s worth it. You have to take off your shoes when you get to the top as well as be wearing something past your knees, so maybe take a pair of socks to protect your feet from the scorching hot floor and a sarong to wrap around your waste to cover up. Definitely worth a visit.
title: Impressive

body: We went there to see the Sunset !It was such a amazing experience we had during our trip in Sri Lanka !Our hotel was very close by to the hotel , Sundaras Resort & Spa !they even gave us free Trasport to the ticket counter 👍Anyways I wound highly recommend you to visit this place if you in Dambulla or Sigiryia.Try to go there in the evening! Not during the day time !
title: Amazing peace of Art

body: Dambulla Cave Temple is worth visiting place. Its a world heritage site. You get to see paintings related to Gautam Buddha & his life on the ceiling of caves. From top, you also get a superb view of Dambulla Town.
title: Worth visiting Dambulla Cave Temple

body: Go here early to avoid the crowds and the heat. It's a bit of a climb to the Temple but it is worth it for the amazing paintings.
title: Just amazing!

body: Like all sites in Sri Lanka, it's either going to be hot or very hot so just be prepared. The complex is up some stairs but our guide took us to an entry that did not appear to be too strenuous a climb to the caves itself. Having a guide makes all the difference to help through interpretation, tipping re footwear, just general things. The temples are obvioulsy very popular with tourists so be prepared for the heat and crowds. Don't feed the monkeys no matter if there are people selling food for them.
title: A fascinating temple complex to visit

body: A must see. A fairly good hike up stairs to the caves in the mountain top. The temples are just breathtaking. Start with the Temple at the far end, and work back, saving the best for last. We visited on a VERY hot day and the stone plaza and walk ways were burning hot. Have socks available to wear and save damage to your feet. Temple guides are available for a fee, if desired, but will take "no" for an answer if you don't need the help. Very happy we saw this while in Sri Lanka.
title: Fascinating and oh, so beautiful!

body: We made a short visit to this cave temple on way to Sigiriya. It was historic and magnificent and is still used as place of worship. Entrance fee for adult is LKR1,500/- each. As it was a religious public holiday, we saw many worshippers too and walked up to the temple with one family who showed us the way. I tried to walk barefoot with them but was too much for me. They told me it was okay to wear my shoes up and took it off before entering the temple. We left our shoes at the shoes counter for LKR25/- a pair, no tickets are issued for this but the man with fuzzy hair assured us not to worry as he would remember whose shoes they belong to. Alternatively, you can leave your shoes in the open at your own risk. There are many Buddha statues in the various caves, a bit dark inside the caves but interesting sights to see how this worship place for many centuries are within the caves.
title: Interesting visit

body: A short hike up the hill, the Dambulla cave temples are a really great place to be. As it is a working temple, you need to be covered shoulders and below the knees, and take off your shoes when you get there, but this is normal practice around Sri Lanka. The 5 temples are cut into the side of the rock - put there by different kings across time, to show their devotion to Buddhism. Do beware of the "guides" that will talk you through the first cave and then offer to take you around the others in return for payment - you can just say no and they will leave you alone.They are beautiful, the detail and differences between them is amazing. There is also a bag drop in the Buddhist book centre at the bottom of the hill so if you come with travelling backpacks you can leave them there!
title: Interesting temples, beautiful and peaceful

body: An impressive Buddhist temple in caves on top of a high hill, accessible by a long steep staircase. Worth a visit.
title: Interesting rock temple

body: It is a 30 minute climb from parking lot. It is recommended to do it when it is not too hot. Also visitors are required to cover knees and sleeveless tops are not allowed. It is ok to put a temporary cloth to cover up to get inside and it can be rented from the ticket counter person at the top of the hill for a small fee. It is very peaceful and nice experience to see so many statues inside the caves.
title: Amazing experience

body: Pictures are no longer a trusted source. This temple was not as beautiful as expected. There's a long and steep walk, hence it's quite important to wear the right shoes. Women must cover their legs and arms. A simple wrap around will do the work. There are 5 temples once you're on top. The pond with lotus growing in them is quite pretty. But it's a very average place.
title: Below expectations

body: Very interesting site. As a temple dress restrictions apply No shoes but socks are worthwhile. Our guide gave us a detailed explanation which certainly helped with an understanding of this very old site
title: Worth the climb

body: Sadly didn’t have enough time to spend at this destination. But would gladly put it on the list for our next visit to Sri Lanka.
title: We passed by en route to Kandy but would return

body: To get to the temple you have to take a tuk tuk from Dambulla, expect to pay around 250-300 LKR. Bargain if they ask for more. Get your tickets at the office before you start climbing up stairs or you'll have to go back down and you really don't want that. The stairs are not too steep but it's being the hottest April in Sri Lanka in 140 years... So if you're planning on going April-May 2019 make sure you take enough water. There's a juice bar near the entrance and after that NOTHING, so again, bring plenty of water and a hat. Socks are recommended cause the floor gets very hot and you have to lose your shoes. The caves are nice, totally worth going, specially if you come from another culture where you never get to see budist temples. If you want to see the Buddha of the Golden Temple, go down the stairs right next to the shoe keeper.
title: Go first thing in the morning.

body: Absolutely stunning visit. Our driver/guide talked us through the story of the temple, explained the paintings and ceremonies. A place not to miss.
title: Incredible place.

body: Certainly worth a visit when visiting the region and can be easily included as part of a visit to Sigiriya etc. The frescos and Buddha shrines are located in the series of caves and are can be seen quite well from the lighting supplied. Flash photography is not condoned so taking pictures can be a challenge. You will have to remove your shoes and have clothes that cover your legs and shoulders.
title: Well worth a visit

body: The cave temple was an amazing stop on our trip. The temples are impressive and fascinating. I would recommend wearing socks because you need to remove your shoes. It just makes walking over the hot stones more comfortable.
title: Pretty Amazing

body: For a start this is a rock ledge ,not a cave.It is a long walk up and as it was lunchtime it was really hot and you must have armpits and knees covered.Maybe I've seen better buddhist sites in thailand and nepal but I was not that amazed.
title: Ok,not that impressed

body: A path upwards of some 250 steps is the way to this site. Hot walk! Site is crowded and interesting once there.
title: Suitable for the fit

body: Short walk up a steep set of stairs and you will reach the beautiful cave temple. There are five cave temples, all subtlety different and individual in their own ways.Costs 1500lkr to enter, plus 25lkr to keep your shoes whilst you enter the temple. But for the history and the beauty well worth the fee.
title: Worth the trip to Dambulla

body: we visit the place on the way to Sigiriya from Colombo,morning time(9.00 am-10.00 am) is good to climb the rock,otherwise rock heat is high,we had to climb nearly about 1/2 hrs,then we entered the cave,amazing,with Buddha statues(standing,meditation ,sleeping buddha statues were there,),inside cave was painted attractivelyancient people creation,out side cave we saw nice sky view,
title: had a great trip to Dambulla

body: This site contains over 100 buddha statues located in a series of shallow caves. Access is via a flight of over 100 steps (or the adjacent service road). They are stunning and magnificent. Mind, we did witness how this has been achieved - they are repainted. If you are able, a must see site. But do try to visit when it is cooler and quieter
title: Very interesting, important site

body: I got a guide who explained each of the caves and as i had visited some other sites the history had made sense. You see the progression in the artwork of the statues of the Buddha.
title: Another really important historic site

body: The climb up could be a challenge for some - My count was 393 uneven stone steps up. Aim for the cooler part of the day and take water. A couple of t shirt sellers along the way, but no hard sell. The view is lovely. As per usual no shoes inside. Just leave outside or pay a small amount to store them. Inside you'll see dozens of ancient Buddha statues(up to 45') and ancient murals. Quite impressive.
title: Unique tribute to Buddha.

body: At times, especially on the climb to the top, this site is ramshackle and dilapidated. Cons and grifters line the route. Need a ticket? Go back down to the gate, avoid the snake-charmer, pay to ride a tuk tuk to the ticket office, then ride back. At the top, every stop "holy men" panhandle for "donations". That being said, once inside the actual caves, they are absolutely amazing. The plaster painted walls look like draped tapestries wrapped over the rocks. Beautiful attention to detail hides among the penny-pinching hustling.
title: Stunning and Ramshackle

body: Quite quiet when we went. Quite a climb up steps to the caves. Have to take shoes off at top before going in complex so best to wear socks as stone surface is very hot if in sun.Lots of statues of budha in the caves and fabulous paintings. Great view from top over countryside
title: Great statutes of Budha

body: A hand held fan salesman would make a fortune here. To reach the temple, you must climb many steps and if you came at midday I imagine this would be very difficult! That said, the Cave Temples were fascinating and worth the walk. There are 5 caves to visit, however restoration work was being carried out on one during our visit so we couldn't see it.
title: Hot, hot, hot!

body: You have to climb many steps and steep inclines to reach the temples but they are well worth it. To see the numerous Buddhas, so different and so colourful is breathtaking and to see how they have cut into the rocks to form the temples is truly mind blowing. Deffo worth a day out.
title: Wear comfy Trainers

body: It's a bit of a hike - about 200 steps - to get to the top, but it's worth it. The statues are incredibly colorful and well-preserved. The five caves differ in size and in the number of Buddhas, but they all have something special to offer.Don't miss the Dambulla Cave Temple!One bit of advice - take an extra pair of socks. As with any temple, you'll have to take your shoes off before entering, but the ground and the walkways between the caves can get VERY HOT, so bring a pair of socks to slip on. Also, go early in the day to avoid the crowds and the heat.
title: Bring socks!

body: Small but filled with spirituality. Incredibly well preserved statues and incredible different techniques. Some of the statues are made from a single rock, some assembled right inside, some of wood hundreds and thousands of years ago. Very important to have a guide, it’s not worth it without one. You will not understand anything. Every posture of Buda means something else and you need someone to tell you about this. It’s cheap, quiet and chill.
title: Don’t miss it

body: you have to climb many steps to reach the temple to see the many faces of the Buddha, but it is worth it, remember to buy your tickets downstairs, as they do not sell tickets at the entrance
title: climbing high

body: There are 5 caves, each with paintings and statues of the Buddha, but to get there you have to climb a lot of uneven steps. They are worth the trek but as with all the tourist sites we have visited so far, they are heaving with tourists.
title: Worth the 200 steps to get there

body: Dambulla Cave Temple also known as Golden Temple is a really beautiful Buddhist temple in Dambulla. You have to climb the rock but view is beautiful, and old caves with statues are amazing. There are alot of monkeys around this area, They will grab your food, bags, mobiles, even flowers. So better keep this in mind when you visit this place. You can't wear shorts or sleeveless tops for temples in Sri Lanka.🐒🐒🌺🌺
title: Golden Temple - Cave Temple

body: As with all the temples in Sri Lanka they are beautiful and the history is breathtaking - go early as if you leave it too late you are with the hordes of tourists buses! Also wear trainer socks as you have to leave your shoes outside and the ground gets really hot!
title: Crazy busy

body: This was one of the best things in Sri Lanka. On top of a hill (a bit of a climb), there are five temples within caves, some dating back over a thousand years. There are many elaborate statues of the Buddha and artefacts alongside. A really beautiful sight with gardens alongside and a lovely walk down to the new temple
title: Stunning group of temples

body: This was a visit whilst on a tour of Sri Lanka. I was looking forward to this. There is a small climb to the top which is not too strenuous for most. The caves are fantastic and hard to believe they are man made. The history is incredible and all the caves are worthy of a visit. Hard to believe the paintings and Buddhas in the caves.The views are also good from the top. You can also have a blessing whilst there.It is worth rembering that shoulders and knees must be covered and no shoes allowed when you go through the entrance.
title: Fantastic caves of Dambulla

body: This place is unbelievable. The paintings are brights despite being centuries old...they look like fabric hanging from a ceiling. The carvings are beautiful. There's definitely a sense of of peace in the temple and on the rock outside. Worth the climb!
title: Is this place real??? (the answer is yes)

body: We thought that the cave is at ground level but it is wrong. You have to walk up around 10-15 minutes. You cannot enter if you wear shorts. The floor is super hot at day time so socks are good options.The cave is not big but very beautiful.
title: The cave is on top of the hill

body: Impressive temples. Worth a visit and.... the climb. In the last one, there was an agressive high pith tone. It hurted my ears, while the others did not hear anything Strange.
title: Impressive

body: The sculptures are exqusite with history...the monkeys on d lookout to snatch whatever possible.And the climb with so much landscape around unbeleivable.....after this tiring episode was releived to find a quiet place serving excerlent cooling refreshing beverages n Excerlent Asian fusion food at such affordable prices.....well worth a trip down or on route to Sigiriya....the name of the place is Laki's Lounge on the Trinco rd, Dambulla......
title: Dambulla cave temple

body: A well preserved cave temple set in 5 sections by separate entrance. Climb a steady uphill to get to the complex mostly steps up & then down:)A combination of statues in various poses & sizes as well as many colorful paintings. Considering how old they are, going back well over a thousand years, that’s pretty impressive. Can spend a good hour plus to enjoy this site. Many tourists combine this with the equally impressive Sigiriya Rock fortress nearby, that can be seen from the top of this location !
title: Lots of Buddha Statues (153 to be precise)

body: If you climbed the 1200 steps of Sigiriya, than these 450 steps are easy for you to reach the top. Like all temples, there is a dress code. Inside this cave temple you find great sculptures. Pay also attention to the ceilings. They are very nice decorated.On your way down to the street you see a huge golden buddha. Entrance fee is Rs1500 for foreigners. This is a very interesting site.
title: Great cave temple complex

body: Made a special trip here based on TA reviews and very glad we made the effort. Three very different caves the last one of which used to be a store room before being converted. The reclining Buddha which had been carved out of the granite is truly wonderful. The effort required to carve the granite with what we a know as very primitive tools must have been immense. Our guide talked us through each cave and the history surrounding it.One piece of advice, we ate in the cafe by The Foreigners car park, the food was amazing. Two Rotis and a bottle of water 150 rupees, its government funded which is why it’s so cheap.
title: Fascinating Three Caves.

body: This temple is worth a visit due to the sheer feat that was involved in constructing it.You will need to leave your shoes outside (Rs50/pair to be stored) and you will need to be covered up as you would expect.The stairs up are quite steep in places and there were many people taking a rest at certain points. The view from the top is beautiful and worth the hike just to see that.You would struggle to spend more than an hour here as there is not a lot more than my pictures show.
title: Interesting

body: We arrived at the site about 2.0clock , steep climb up about 500 steps to the caves. At the top you need to take off your shoes. But the tiles outside are incredibly hot. Tip is to take socks with you to put on when you take your shoes off.It is worth the visit especially with a guide
title: Steep climb but worth it

body: All you need is approx. 2 hours and a long flight of steps with an awesome view to explore these interesting caves of religious history. I was more fascinated on how these statues were placed in these caves. Note that you need to be covered from your shoulders to your ankles as a respect. Just a pareo or a sarong should suffice. Ladies no baring of shoulders please. You must leave your foot wear outside the temples. There is a fee for keeping your sandals safe. Less than USD$1. Don't leave your sandals unattended cos the monkeys will take it.
title: Interesting Religious History

body: Lots of steps but worth the effort. As per the other reviewers, try to go early as the sun heats up the rocks you need to walk on. You have to pay to store your shoes to just before you go into the temples so allow 50 rupees for each set of shoes.Caves are amazing!
title: Amazing

body: Worth visiting if you are passing by the temple as you can gain some knowledge about history and specially enjoy the ancient paintings. Make sure to go in the early morning or in an evening as the scorching sun can burn you during the walk to the cave temple from the vehicle. However, it is not worthy to make your plans purposely to visit this temple itself. Just take a visit if you are passing by.
title: A Historical Place

body: This is a very interesting temple with an amazing history. Get a guide.There are a number of steps up from the car park but they are level and easy walking. There are five temples to see each with different statues, rock carvings and wall paintings.The views are stunning, the temple flowers beautiful and the monkeys delightful.In the car park is a cafe (of sorts) and toilets. Look out for the "Jack fruit" tree with the amazing and very large Jack fruits. Tasty too.
title: Lots of steps but worth it.

body: There are a number of cave temples, most of the Bhuddist but one is Hindu. We had a monk show us around well worth the small charge. In spite of the large numbers of people the site remains tranquil. Watch out for the monkeys
title: A hard climb but worth it

body: World Heritage Site, beautiful and very interesting temples, bit of a walk up but worth it when you get to the top.You have to take your shoes off so socks are useful !
title: Excellent

body: Steps rise steeply from the car park for approx 100m. Sari hire (for those who need to cover knees approx 100SLK). Three main caves to explore. Return to car park avoiding steep steps possible half way down far side (right at shop). Golden temple easier to reach by road rather than walking.
title: Very steep climb - for temple enthusiasts!

body: Wear good walking shoes to climb the rocky stairs and socks to manage the hot stones after you leave your shoes at the entrance- take your time to look at the ceilings and the statues- very rich!
title: Well worth it

body: The hike up to the caves is by a longish flight of steps and takes about 20 minutes. There is an extensive array of Buddha statues and painted images (>150) many of which are interesting. We were unfortunate to arrive at a time when the caves were closed for prayers and so a large number of visitors accumulated outside the caves waiting to be admitted, which meant the caves became extremely crowded and difficult to move around once they reopened - I imagine it would be much less of a problem if you are able to arrive some time after the caves have been reopened (unfortunately I do not know when the prayer times are).
title: Worth the climb

body: For almost $8 a visit and with so many visitors, you’d think these caves could be properly maintained. They aren’t properly lit, the outsides are crumbling and wooden tables keep the visitors back. Touts bother you a lot. There is zero information on the caves around the site. No signs to the golden temple (which we almost missed). Disappointing.
title: Nice caves, shame they are not maintained

body: You don't need a guide, just a guide book to appreciate the history and beauty of the cave temples. You will need to wear clothes that cover your knees and your shoulders. Don't be one of those disrespectful tourists that hasn't bothered and has to borrow a sarong. Also, it's worth wearing socks - you are asked to take your shoes off but the rock paving is very hot by the afternoon and hard to walk on in bare feet - socks help!The temples date back to the 1st century BC and there is evidence of settlement here before that. The main attractions are 5 caves full of ancient Buddhist frescos and Buddha statues. Because they have been protected from sunlight the colours are vivid and beautiful. The whole place is very peaceful and relaxing - enjoy. Also, there are lots of monkeys outside who provide great entertainment!
title: Stunning frescos and carvings, peaceful, spiritual place.

body: Dambulla is the largest and best preserved cave complex in Sri Lanka. Very decorative and very interesting. There are a total of 153 BUDDHA Statues. These painting and Statues are related to BUDDHA and his life. 153 buddha Statues, Sri Lankan Kings, gods and goddesses Statues. This an impressive and interesting place to visit. it's almost incomprehensible the massive and creative work Statues and painting
title: "Rich Story Of Sri Lanka"

body: A long set of steps up to the top but worth it, take your time. Amazing place goes back to 1st century BC, lots of temples built into the granite rock, some now under restoration but still accessible. Incredible ceiling paintings all telling stories, Stunning views of the countryside included. Definitely a high light of Sri Lanka
title: Worth the climb take a deep breath

body: We went to see cave temple which is fascinating, even more if you learned about the history of the place. Definitely worth a visit. However choose time of the visit carefully as you will walk around barefoot. You should go early in the morning when it’s not that hot. The entrance fee is 3000 rupees for 2 adults and 2 children and extra 25 rupees per pair of shoes which you need to leave outside. When you are finished proceed to Golden temple.
title: This is why you visit Dambulla

body: Climb 221 steps and take in the grandeur of Buddha carvings and paintings from a forevone era. Marvel at the golden Buddha. Be quiet and respect meditating monks. It’s another world like movies about ancient past and you are sure to be transported to times and eras now lost in history and fiction. Keep three hours at least if not more. Climb slowly resting all the while. Then take in Buddha in his glorified carvings on the walls. Out of this world experience.
title: Lifetime experience

body: It's almost incomprehensible to think about the massive and creative work that was involved in building this extraordinary rock sanctuary. I'm not a Buddhist, but I very much appreciated seeing the golden temples, statues, grottoes and wall paintings. This was one of the stops on the Gate1 tour that I was on, and I'm pleased that this UNESCO World Heritage site was included on the tour.
title: Amazing UNESCO site

body: A very clean and neat Cave Temple in Dambulla but a word of warning to the elderly and any one with cardiac or breathing problems. The steps are over 200, uneven on a stony surface. there are stretches with no hand rails and the descent is equally telling on the knees. However the climb is finally worthwhile. Statues of Buddha bring serenity all around. Washrooms charge a lot available on descending. Must have is coconut water available all over the country. About SL Rupee 80/- for tourists. Choose the orange variety.
title: Climbing at 72

body: The only thing I can say on this place is AWESOME.You can't go in Sri Lanka and don't visit Dambulla Caves
title: AWESOME PLACE

body: A complex of five Buddhist temples carved into the rocks. All are fascinating. The first has a huge reclining Buddha statue and the next two each have 50 or more different statues. Make sure you leave your shoes at the entrance (25 rupees a pair).
title: Fascinating place

body: Cave paintings dating from 1st century and onwards, together with hundreds of Buddha statues make this an impressive and interesting place to visit. There are, however, many steps to climb before you reach them, giving magnificent views over the surrounding countryside.
title: Cave paintings

body: There are a lot of reviews in the wrong place here and Trip Advisor should sort them out.The Dambulla Cave Temple is a must-see and probably the best sight in Sri Lanka. Despite the steep climb, though you will be accompanied by well-mannered monkeys, it is worth the effort and really spectacular. There are six caves but each is separate and not very deep so you can come out to cool off it is gets too hot. The usual shoes off, though the floors are fairly clean, and cover shoulders and knees. Trips usually start at the ticket office and return the other way past the Golden Temple.
title: This is in Dambulla not in Habarana and is different from the Golden Temple, Dambulla.

body: Entry Fees: LKR 1500 per person for foreign nationalsThere are 3 different entry points. But there is only one ticket booking office. The entry point from the Golden Temple is most painful if you dont have the tickets. From here you will have to first climb a bit, then get down, take the tickets and climb back again.Easiest option is go from the back side, pick the tickets from the booking office and get down at the next gate. From there the climb is lesser. Also there arent steps to climb from here. So slightly easier. You may be able to spot "Giant squirrel" if you are lucky. There are loads of monkeys near the cave and they snatch food. So be careful.The caves are good and maintained well. I met lot of crowd there.It can be done if you have time. But would recommend to visit in the morning hours.
title: Visit during morning hours

body: well worth a trip to see the various caves and statue but if you can get a guide as the rooms can be quite complicated to understand, go early to avoid crowds or you may struggle to get in some rooms which are quiet small. Very decorative and very interesting. You can get access from the car park half way up if going by coach to avoid most of the steps from the entrance
title: amazing sights

body: Dambulla cave temple is an excellent way to while a way an hour or two? There are lots of steps to get to the entrance so I would suggest you should be reasonably fit and healthy to enter but once in the temple areas, Buddhas and fresco pairings are marvellous. Our guide explained many things to us whilst there which helped us understand the importance of particular things, but with or without a guide it’s a must see. It’s amazing these beautiful things were created so long ago and still exist today. Definitely worth a visit but things to beat in mind are that can be very hot in the caves, and always leave you shoes with the ‘shoe guy’. It only cost 20r to ensure they are there when you get out?
title: Stunning

body: An important religious and cultural site. The climb is nothing compared with Lions Rock. The caves are all highly decorated and very interesting. One was being restored but you could still go in and it was interesting to see the team of conservators at work.
title: Very interesting

body: We went early so was not crowded when we went up. They have a room where you can keep the luggage and when you arrive to the top they have a clock room for shoes in exchange for a fee. The temple is nice and the handwork impressive. We had the opportunity of seeing the paintings of a room being restaured and then you realised how hard work is everywhere. Nice view also from the top
title: Nice place

body: Worth the trek up the steps. Stunning views along the way with plenty of places to stop and enjoy the vistas. Amazing statutes, intricate design and colours. Remember to wear your socks as the ground gets hot!
title: Worth the trek

body: We liked this place more than Kandy (if I may compare apples and oranges). We did as the Rough Guide recommended, i.e., started visiting the ‘caves’ from the one furthest from the entrance (cave 5, the smallest one), building the momentum up to cave 2 (the greatest) and cave 1 for the dessert. I use the scare quotes around ‘caves’, as they are not real caves, but a space under a hanging rock partitioned into five areas. Very atmospheric place. The entrance (for foreigners) is 1500 LKR, with additional 25 LKR for each pair of shoes you leave in a safety shack just before entering the caves. Worth the climb.
title: better than Kandy

body: There are two paths up to the caves. One has steps the other a steep slope. We didn’t fancy the steps so went the other way, which I believe takes a bit longer. It was a bit of a trek, but fine, definitely worth it to see the cave temple. It’s amazing how tranquil they are considering the crowds. There are 5 caves in all. The first one is tiny so some patience (and queuing) is needed. The second one is huge and the third is pretty big too. When you’ve seen those three you’ve seen the best of it and the other caves are just more of the same. Remember to cover your shoulders and knees. Take a pair of socks because you can’t wear shoes inside. They will look after your shoes outside the entrance for 50Sr a pair. Otherwise take a bag and carry them around. Also, most importantly don’t pose for pictures with your back to Budda, it’s a big no no. The path to the left on the way down leads you to the Golden Temple Of Dambulla, with its giant Budda, which is worth seeing just by itself. Overall this was definitely worth the trek and we’re happy we saw this impressive cave temple. Iain, London
title: Definitely worth the trek

body: Not so great, USD 7 entry ticket, too much crowd,It is having many top ceiling drawings, other than, no much special attraction
title: family visit

body: It's a must when travelling from Habarana to Kandy or the opposite ...The scenery around the Temple is attractive.... The frescoes and the sculptures are brilliant,... Still t's no art but profund devotion ! We enjoyed there a great moment of spirituality.
title: Don't miss it !!

body: If you are OK with the high number of steps, and warm, inside you are for a treat. This collection of 5 caves with their internal paintings has been carved in the rock. It is very busy and photography is not easy. But it is definately worth visiting
title: Amazing

body: What a great treat this was. About three hundred steps you reach this amazing five cave Temple complex. The statues and ceiling art are beautiful. A very much must see. Its very hot so bring plenty of water and an extra pair of socks for walking the grounds. Long pants and sleeved shirts are required. Absolutely stunning.
title: Vacation

body: An impressive collection of statues. We really enjoyed this visit. Very atmospheric rooms carved into the side of the mountain full of beautiful buddhas.
title: Fascinating

body: Dambulla cave temple also known as the Golden Temple of Dambulla is a World Heritage Site in Sri Lanka. The largest and best-preserved cave temple complex major attractions are spread over five caves, which contain statues and paintings. These paintings and statues are related to Gautama Buddha and his life. There are a total of 153 Buddha statues, three statues of Sri Lankan kings and four statues of gods and goddesses. The latter include Vishnu and the Ganesha. The murals cover an area of 2,100 square metres. Depictions on the walls of the caves include the temptation by the demon Mara, and Buddha's first sermon.Entrance Cost: 1500RsShoes Deposit: 25Rs
title: A MUST TO VISIT IF YOU IN DAMBULLA

body: but be warned -360 stairs to reach the caves - but totally worth it and there are losts of resting places
title: Awe inspiring but strenuous!

body: We visited here mid morning when the temperature was a little cooler. A 300+ step climb to the top but well worth it, we felt. The caves are impressive, as are the carvings, and the atmosphere is very tranquil despite the number of visitors. Some great views from the top too!
title: Beautiful place!

body: Definitely a must to see. Nice to be out of the heat and in the caves, but still it is very humid. You need to be respectful and hat and shoes are taken off. Make sure and check out the ceilings as well.
title: Amazing!

body: We visited the temple because our private driver recommended it to us. You have to buy the ticket for 1500 rupees and walk up the stairs. On top there is someone you have to pay to watch your shoes and if you dont wear long pants or a long skirt they won't let you in. There is someone waiting for those people to borrow a sheet to cover your knees, but afterwards he wants 100 rupees...The temple is not that spectacular...
title: Very expensive...

body: We visited these temples in the afternoon and started the 300 or so step climb up the King's way about 4:30pm. It was a bit of an effort because of the heat and the unevenness of the steps. A couple of stops on the way up to observe the monkeys and take in the views helped. The whole area around the temples was intriguing and scenic - after all its not every day you see such intricate paintings set in such an environment. You can take photos but not with flash so phone cameras do quite well here. We decended on the opposite side of the rock which takes you into the Golden Temple that houses the giant budda. We were also able to view Lion rock in the distance and teh nable to do this in reverse the following day at Sirigiya. Worth a short visit as it is unusual.
title: A bit of a hidden gem

body: Wow !! This is an breathtaking site. We truly were awed by what we. It’s easy to spend a lot if time here. Bring a flashlight as it will help you see in some of the darker portions. Don’t miss it !
title: Stunning

body: I climbed up the 364 steps and found that there is actually another way up slope without having to climb so many steps. When I reached the top, it was drizzling and the guard was very kind to allow me to sit down to rest in one of their chairs and even offered me some water as I am totally exhausted and feeling giddy/ after the climb. Remember to bring a bag to keep your shoes inside your bag or carry it around without having to store with others' shoes. Many tourists had to use the scarf provided as the guards are pretty strict about covered sholder and over-knee attire. Honestly speaking I find that this place is over-rated after the diffiicult climb. Been a South-East Asian, I have seen all kinds of temples so there is nothing special for me here except the structure of the building under the rock. Maybe unless one is Buddhist then it may be a must to see Otherwise, I will gladly give it a miss.
title: Overrated for the climb

body: The steps up to the cave are steep but the distance is short and it's well worth the effort when you get to the top.I'm not keen on walking bare foot )stubbed my toe) but you have to observe local customs. There are over 150 images of the Buddha painted on the walls of the five caves - impressive.
title: Worth the effort

body: The climb is worthwhile and the 5 caves holing the Buddhas are different but all good in their own way.
title: Outstanding

body: It is just another place of statues and paintings of 1st century BC. However, the paintings and statues were repaired and repainted in 11th, 12th, and 18th century AD. These caves were the place where Buddhist monks were meditating. This rock temple built by King Valagamba in the 1st century BC. Very disappointing to see that there is no proper lighting, cleanliness and guide service at the caves. In spite of collecting entry fees no enough attention is given to the visitors. Serious efforts are required to bring back the glorious past to the caves, statues and the surroundings.
title: Worth a visit

body: A lot of steps! Needs some effort to reach it but caves and the view are really worth it! Entrance fee is LKR 1500, fee for shoes storing is LKR 25 per pair. Temple is functioning, you can here monks singing in the morning and in the evening if stay in the nearby hotels
title: Interesting!

body: The temple is situated at the top of a steep hill and several older/less fit struggled to climb it comfortably in the oppressive heat, but once there the paintings/statuary are quite stunning.
title: Very interesting, worth the climb!

body: If you have travelled much around South-east Asia you will have seen all of this before, often better and probably for free. Sure, the setting is a novelty with the temples set inside five decorated caves and there are an incredible number of Buddha statues but, fundamentally, there is little to set the place apart. We had anticipated a series of caverns but the caves are actually 5 individual units. Inside each the lighting is subdued and, as a result, the whole atmosphere is gloomy and uninspiring. We have visited many, many temples in the likes of Thailand, Myanmar and Cambodia, generally without charge, and seen some stunning interiors. Sadly this place didn’t live up to those standards.On a practical level, the ticket office is located a considerable distance from the road which makes for a significant walk (for those arriving independently) before you even begin the climb up the hill. Enter at the Golden Temple, follow the sign for the Cave Temple and just keep going until, eventually, you get to the ticket office. At 1500 rupees we felt the entry charge was way too much for what is on offer. Also, remember to take a sarong or else you will have to hire one there at additional charge (including men if you’re wearing shorts).
title: Disappointing

body: Interesting Temple. It is quite different from the other that we have seen but to be honest the ticket price for foreigners is too expensive for a 20 minutes attraction. However, it remained as a good memory in our minds. They should do something with the touts inside who are pushy and try to give you different explanations in exchange of some money.
title: Overrated

body: You will need to take a bottle of water with you and it's a 700 step climb to the top, which in humidity of 80% is a bit tiring. We enjoyed the visit and a guide showed us around. The colours of the paintings are incredible - they look like they were done yesterday and are 1300 years or more old.. a must visit .
title: Very interesting visit...

body: Another of the must places to visit and yes more steep steps to climb as they always seem to be at the top of a hill. There are 5 caves to visit of different size, and it is suggested that you go in reverse order, 5 to 1. The ceiling painting is fantastic and there are lots of buddhas of varying size. We went at 0900 on leaving Kandy and the visit lasted 2 hours.
title: Part of Sri Lanka's rich history

body: We were in dambulla for 2 complete days even if you can do it on a 1day rush trip.We managed to hire a great tuk-tuk driver o took us to everywhere nearby the city and more... Through rural areas and off the beaten track areas.Dambulla caves were the first Stop on the Sunset of our first day. Amazing time to visit this really charming place.They have 5 different small temples wich are full of statues and a Nice surrounding área.If you need a good tuk-tuk driver for hoje Stay in Dambulla here is our driver phone Number: Sunil 0776178324
title: Dambulla tuk-tuk

body: Incredible place, well worth the unexpectedly long climb up!! The architecture was breath taking and images and paintings beautiful. When you consider how old this place is, it makes it even more special!Take plenty of water as there is none on sale at the top and be prepared to say no to all the sellers waiting outside.There is a stand for looking after shoes which cost 25 SLR per pair plus a tip, but there are places to leave your shoes if you're stingy!!
title: Dambulla Cave Temples

body: A mesmerising experience. Each cave has its own character, containing beautifully carved and painted statues. The atmosphere inside is like that of an Indiana Jones movie. Also good to see the worshippers bringing their offerings.
title: A long climb, but worth it.

body: Another must-see attraction in the Dambulla area. And another steep climb - about 300 steps. The five cave temples are from different time periods and varying styles. All very interesting. Large areas roped off to avoid destruction. Crowds can make the smaller caves claustrophobic. Go as early as possible. We saw this the same day as Sigiriya. If possible do on two separate days - quite exhausting to do both!
title: Fascinating

body: This complex is well worth seeing even though there are quite a few steps to climb to reach it not all of which are even. There are several caves with many figures within them and the lighting makes it very atmospheric.
title: An Interesting Visit

body: Fascinating rock temple with origin in 1st c. BC is definitely place worth the visit. After taking lots of stairs up the rock, well-deserved view over jungle and distant hills presents itself. Temple that is inbuilt into rock masif is part of world heritage and despite it´s honourable age, statues and cave paintings are well preserved. We arrived late afternoon and we stayed to watch sunset from the top which was wonderful. I really recommend to not skip this place if you visit Sri Lanka. Be prepared for a climb, carying some water with you, covering yourself while entering the temple and also for lots of locals trying to sell you souvenirs. Exiting area is by descending down to Golden Temple which is nice too, pretty new place but what were we more excited about was small stall with delicious local snacks next to it :)
title: Place you should not miss
Amazing statues in a series of temples
body: There is a series of caves from different centuries filled with statues and carvings and rich colours. Well worth a visit and a pleasant 15 minute stroll up to the top,making friends with the monkeys along the way.

title: Dambulla Cave Temple
body: A World Heritage Site in Sri Lanka. The rock towers 160 m over the surrounding plains. It has five caves, which contain statues and paintings. Around 400 steps to climb. Entry fees 1500 slr.

title: Amazing historical site
body: This temple has many chambers or rooms, many Buddha statues and some fantastic painted ceilings. You need a guide to tell you about what you can see as there are not many information panels. Well worth taking time to look at all areas.

title: Awe inspiring statues and cave paintings
body: The main draw to Dambulla is the centuries old Cave Temple. Reached by Tuk Tuk to the ticket office, you can then climb the steps or walk around to the tarmaced sloping path that approaches from the other side. There are several caves, and the guide leaflet is not very informative but hilarious for is inventive use of the English language and its summative table of how many Buddhas in each cave. Take some time to study the statues, and also to look at the painted walls and ceilings. There's a lot to see, so wait for the crush to die down in order to have a really good experience. £ times a day, Buddha is fed, and tourists are ushered out so he can enjoy his meal in peace. This only takes 15 minutes, so enjoy the view outside and speculate on what the dish of the day is! When you've seen enough, walk back down, avoiding the monkeys who wait to steal your fruit and belongings. At the bottom you can also visit the Golden Temple and various other museums. Well worth half a day to really appreciate this site, and enjoy the calm it brings.

title: Budha statues and temple not made in china style ;-)
body: A very nice temple with passion made in the past and without “made in china” plastic tingelings all over. Only minor is that foreigners have to take a totaly different entrance (walk around the whole complex) and like all over sri lanka have to pay 10-100 times more.

title: Spirit of place
body: The walk up is scenic and the steps manageable as you can admire the view and take photos if you need a breather.Go early because it’s cooler and especially at the weekend when the locals will visit to pray.It’s the largest conserved cave temple in Sri Lanka. There are four caves containing statues and painted images of budda. The paintings cover the walls and ceilings and you need to allow your eyes to acclimatise to the dim lighting and then take in the detail. It was pretty busy on the Sunday morning that we visited and the caves were humid and full of visitors trying to get the perfect shot which created some bottle necks. Then, in the midst of all the tourist footfall, there were the local worshippers making their offerings which helped to remind you what this place is really all about. It’s worth taking some quiet time to soak up the atmosphere and to enjoy the place before heading back down.Dress modestly, remove your shoes and turn off the flash.

title: Good walk, unusual temple.
body: The Dambulla Cave Temple is located on top of a mountain and to get to it you need to climb hundreds of steps, so wear appropriate shoes, and also it is a requirement that you wear clothes that cover your knees. The view from the top of the mountain is spectacular. The temples are well worth seeing, set into caves and with an interesting history.

title: Great to learn something about Sri Lanka's history
body: This is an ancient Cave temple that dates back to the 1st century. There are five chambers with murals painted all over the walls and Buddha's carved out of stone. The golden temple is also part of the UNESCO site.Physical challenge: we came up from the cave carpark and there are a lot of steps that are uneven, we saw a lot of older people stopping to take rest along the way. There is some cover, but on a sunny day it was quite intense. The view going up is amazing.Costs: it cost 1500 rupee for the entry ticket. At the temple you must remove your shoes. There is a shoe cloak bay where people look after your shoes for about 50 rupee. I was told shoulders and knees.must be covered. I had shorts to my knees but was still required to hire a wrap to cover the lower part of my legs. Wraps cost 100 rupee to hire

title: Interesting but not great
body: We found the Cave Temple to be of interest. There are 5 caves: start at the one furthest from the entrance and work back - that way you get the best last.,Caves 3-5 are underwhelming but Caves 1&2 are worthwhile.

title: A must
body: Sri Lanka is steeped in history and has some amazing sites. However, there is a danger you can get templed out. If you are only planning to visit a few, this is a must. 5 temples built into the cave through the centuries, dating back to the 1st century. It was amazing to see. You must wear clothing that covers shoulders and knees. Take shoes off. There is a place to leave your shoes but we put them in our ruck sack. You can’t carry your shoes or have them on display. Take water with you, there are only postcards and fridge magnets on sale outside at the top. Only criticism was there was not any information provided. We luckily had a tourist book, it’s with visiting the furthers cave/ temple first and working your way back. Try do a bit of research before you go.
